_meta.purpose: Sourced etymologies of Indian place names — how each got its name, and when the name is first attested. Sourced-or-gap: a claim is cited or marked a gap; contested origins are flagged, not resolved. Most names are ancient (BCE/early CE).
_meta.honesty: Etymology is often contested; where scholars differ we say so and cite the reading rather than pick a winner. 'First attested' = the earliest surviving text/inscription that records the name, not necessarily when it was coined.

places.name: Kashmir
places.origin: From Sanskrit Kaśmīra. The Nilamata Purana derives it from the sage Kashyapa (Kaśyapa) draining the vast lake Satisar — 'Kaśyapa-mira/mera', the land the sage reclaimed from water. Kalhana's Rajatarangini (12th c.) records the same tradition. A folk gloss reads 'ka' (water) + 'shimir' (to desiccate) = land dried out of water.
places.attested_note: Recorded as Kaspeiria (Ptolemy, 2nd c. CE) and in the Ashokan-era Buddhist accounts; the drained-lake tradition is Puranic.

places.name: Bharat
places.meaning: Land of the Bharatas / of Bharata
places.origin: From the Bharata clan/king of the Rigveda — the Bharatas are a Rigvedic people, and 'Bhāratavarṣa' is the land of Bharata. Later tradition names it for Emperor Bharata (Rishabha's son in Jain accounts; Dushyanta & Shakuntala's son in the Mahabharata).
places.attested_note: The Bharatas appear in the Rigveda's 'Battle of the Ten Kings'; 'Bhāratavarṣa' is Puranic.

places.name: India
places.origin: From the river Sindhu → Old Persian Hindu → Greek Indos → Latin India. The Greeks named the land beyond the Indus after the river.
places.attested_note: Herodotus (c. 440 BCE) uses 'Indos' for the river and its people; Darius I's inscriptions record 'Hi(n)du' as a satrapy.

places.name: Hindustan
places.meaning: Land of the Hindu (Indus) / of the Indus people
places.origin: Persian: Hindū (from Sindhu) + -stān ('land'). Coined in the Persianate world for the land of the Indus and, later, the northern plains.
places.attested_note: 'Hindustan' appears in Sasanian Persian; widened under the Delhi Sultanate & Mughals.

places.name: Delhi
places.origin: Traditionally from Raja Dhilu (c. 1st c. BCE); an Apabhramsha reading is 'dhili' (loose) for a loose iron pillar. The early name 'Dhillika' is recorded on a 12th-c. inscription. The site is old — Indraprastha of the Mahabharata is placed here.
places.attested_note: Earliest firm epigraphic form is 12th c.; the Dhilu tradition is legendary.

places.name: Maharashtra
places.origin: Sanskrit mahā ('great') + rāṣṭra ('nation, realm'). An alternate reading ties it to 'Maharashtri' Prakrit or to the Rathi/Ratta people (mahā-rathi, 'great charioteers').
places.attested_note: Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) records 'Mo-ho-la-ch'a' (Maharashtra) in the 7th c.; the term appears earlier in Prakrit.

places.name: Karnataka
places.origin: From Kannada karu ('lofty/black') + nāḍu ('land') — 'the lofty land' or 'land of black soil'. Recorded historically as 'Karnata desha'.
places.attested_note: 'Karnata' appears in the Mahabharata; the modern state was named Karnataka in 1973.

places.name: Tamil Nadu
places.meaning: Land of the Tamils / Tamil-speaking land
places.origin: Tamil ('the Tamil language/people') + nāḍu ('land, country'). 'Tamilakam' — the ancient Tamil country — is named in Sangam literature.
places.attested_note: 'Tamilakam' is a Sangam-age term; 'Tamil Nadu' as a modern state name dates to 1969.

places.name: Kerala
places.origin: Popular gloss: keram ('coconut') + alam ('land'). Scholarly reading: from the Chera dynasty — 'Cheralam' → Kerala. The Ashokan Edicts (3rd c. BCE) name 'Keralaputra' (son of the Cheras).
places.attested_note: 'Keralaputo' appears in Ashoka's Rock Edicts II & XIII — one of the oldest surviving records of the name.

places.name: Punjab
places.meaning: Five waters (land of the five rivers)
places.origin: Persian panj ('five') + āb ('water') — the land of the five rivers (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej). The ancient Sanskrit name was 'Sapta Sindhu' (seven rivers).
places.attested: Persianate name from c. 16th c.; region ancient
places.attested_note: 'Panjāb' is a Persianate coinage; the Rigveda's 'Sapta Sindhu' is the older name for the wider region.

places.name: Bengal
places.origin: From Vaṅga, an ancient kingdom/janapada of the eastern Ganges delta; 'Vangala' → Bengal. Possibly from a Dravidian/Austroasiatic root or the Bang tribe.
places.attested_note: Vanga appears in the Aitareya Aranyaka and the Mahabharata; 'Vangaladesa' on the 11th-c. Nesari plates.

places.name: Gujarat
places.origin: From 'Gurjara-rāṣṭra' — the land of the Gurjara people, who established power here in the early medieval period.
places.attested_note: 'Gurjara' appears in the early medieval period (Gurjara-Pratihara era).
